Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second essay! The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. It will be Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma to open the innings for India Women. Darcie Brown will start with the new ball for Australia Women. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ....

Right then, India Women will fancy themselves to chase down this total. It will not be easy against this Aussie bowling unit and they will have to bat smartly to get over the line. Can the Indian batters get the job done and help their side take the lead in the series? We shall find out in a bit.

After being put into bat, Australia Women were off to a steady start courtesy of their openers but both Alyssa Healy and Beth Mooney departed in quick succession. Tahlia McGrath and Ashleigh Gardner followed suit which put them under a lot of pressure. Phoebe Litchfield and Ellyse Perry then got together to steady the ship and did well to keep the scoreboard ticking. Litchfield picked up where she left off in the ODI series while Perry played the second fiddle in that stand. Having gotten a life early in her innings, Litchfield was unable to make it count and fell on 49 which opened the floodgates for India Women. Australia Women just could not gather any momentum as they failed to string any partnerships and were eventually bowled out in the last over.

A sensational bowling performance from India Women! They have rolled Australia Women over for 141 and they will be the happier side going into the halfway mark! The Women in Blue meant business right from the start and it showed on the field. It was just the start India Women were after as Titas Sadhu struck soon after she got into the attack. Renuka Singh got into the act soon after before Sadhu struck twice in an over to pile more misery on the visitors. It was a quiet middle phase for India Women where they gave Phoebe Litchfield a reprieve and allowed Australia Women to stitch a partnership. Amanjot Kaur helped them break that stand and the rest of the bowling unit kept picking wickets at regular intervals to keep Australia Women in check. The pick of the bowlers undoubtedly was Titas Sadhu with her four wickets.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Amanjot Kaur takes her second catch and Shreyanka Patil finishes the innings! She tosses this one up, full and around off, Georgia Wareham backs away to loft it over long off but fails to get the elevation, the ball goes high in the air and Amanjot Kaur there comes forward and takes a comfortable catch. Australia Women have been bowled out for 141!

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Titas Sadhu to Tahlia McGrath, OUT! c Pooja Vastrakar b Titas Sadhu.

Commentary.Commentary: Make that four dots! This is back of a length and on off, Tahlia McGrath looks to punch it away but gets an inside edge onto her pads as the ball goes nowhere. The pressure is building up on McGrath here.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Titas Sadhu to Tahlia McGrath, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just short! Titas Sadhu lands this one on a good length and around off, nips away a bit, Tahlia McGrath looks to push it away from her body but gets an outside edge which falls just in front of Deepti Sharma at first slip. Three dots in a row now!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Titas Sadhu to Tahlia McGrath, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length this time, on middle again, Tahlia McGrath stays back and tucks it towards short mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Titas Sadhu to Tahlia McGrath, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller one and on middle, shaping in, Tahlia McGrath miscues her drive off the toe end of the bat down the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Titas Sadhu to Tahlia McGrath, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Missed out! Back of a length, sliding down leg, there to be put away, Ellyse Perry uses her feet and swings to get it fine on the leg side but misses out. The ball brushes off her pads and rolls towards the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Renuka Singh to Ellyse Perry, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling into the right-hander, on a back of a length, on off, Ellyse Perry stabs it down on the off side for a dot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Renuka Singh to Ellyse Perry, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Serves it on a length, around off, Ellyse Perry stays back in her crease and punches it to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Renuka Singh to Ellyse Perry, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Ellyse Perry comes out to the middle now.

OUT! TAKEN! Renuka Singh strikes now and both Aussie openers go back in quick succession here. She serves this one full and around off, shaping away a bit, Alyssa Healy goes for the big one but only manages to slice it up in the air due to the away movement, Harmanpreet Kaur at mid off once again settles under it and takes another fine catch. India Women on top here!
Commentary.Howout: c Harmanpreet Kaur b Renuka Singh
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Renuka Singh to Alyssa Healy, OUT! c Harmanpreet Kaur b Renuka Singh.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Swung away nicely! On a length and shaping into the batter, Alyssa Healy shimmies down the track and swats it through mid-wicket. Smriti Mandhana runs to her left but cannot cut it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Renuka Singh to Alyssa Healy, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on middle by Renuka Singh, Alyssa Healy firms the drive back to the bowler. Renuka fires in a throw at the batting end which deflects away on the leg side off the batter's pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Renuka Singh to Alyssa Healy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! In the channel on off, on a good length, Tahlia McGrath pokes at the delivery away from her body and gets beaten on the outside edge. End of a successful over from Titas Sadhu!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Titas Sadhu to Tahlia McGrath, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tahlia McGrath walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND GONE! Titas Sadhu draws first blood for India Women! Beth Mooney was looking good during her stay in the middle! Bowls it on a good length from around the wicket, on middle, Beth Mooney shimmies down the track to launch it down the ground but does not get to the pitch of the ball. Skies it high in the air towards mid on where Harmanpreet Kaur back track and keeps her eyes on the ball all the way through. Kaur judges it to perfection and reverse cups it with ease.
Commentary.Howout: c Harmanpreet Kaur b Titas Sadhu
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Titas Sadhu to Beth Mooney, OUT! c Harmanpreet Kaur b Titas Sadhu.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls it full, on off, Beth Mooney drives well but can't get it past cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Titas Sadhu to Beth Mooney, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A confident appeal for caught behind but turned down! There was a noise and India Women have taken the review! Was that bat or pad? Or both? Titas Sadhu gets the ball to shape back into the left-hander, on a good length, on middle, Beth Mooney gets deceived by the sharp movement as she looks to go drive it down the ground. Gets cut in half as the ball sneaks past the inside edge and it is pouched safely by Richa Ghosh diving away to her right. The UltraEdge rolls up but it shows no bat. The on-field decision will stand and India Women lose their review!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Titas Sadhu to Beth Mooney, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good effort in the deep! Sees the batter make room and bowls it away from her, on a length, near the tramline on off, Beth Mooney throws her hands at the delivery and carves it in the air towards third man. Renuka Singh in the deep, runs and dives to her left to save a couple of runs for her side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Titas Sadhu to Beth Mooney, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from around the wicket and goes full in search of swing, outside off, Beth Mooney leans on and drives it crisply but straight to short extra cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Titas Sadhu to Beth Mooney, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! In the channel on off, on a short of a length, Alyssa Healy gives the charge and swings to go back over the bowler's head but connects with thin air.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Renuka Singh to Alyssa Healy, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length delivery, outside off, Beth Mooney stands tall and punches it to deep cover to rotate the strike.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR BYES! That has beaten everyone! Angling away, near the tramline on off, on a length, Beth Mooney shuffles to the off side and shapes herself to scoop it over the keeper but misses out. Richa Ghosh is blind-sighted due to the batter's movement and the ball races past her left glove and into the third man fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, 4 Byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Fine stop! Pulls her length back does Renuka Singh and bowls it outside off, Beth Mooney cuts it from the crease towards backwards point. Jemimah Rodrigues dives low to her left and makes the stop.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Beth Mooney with the first maximum of the T20I series! Renuka Singh serves it up to the batter, outside off, Beth Mooney shuffles across and gets down on one knee. She gets the ball in her arc and slogs it over mid-wicket for a maximum.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: At pace, on a back of a length, outside off, Beth Mooney plays it close to her body and cuts it late but straight to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Angling across the left-hander from over the wicket, on a length, Beth Mooney walks across her stumps and opens herself up to cream the drive to deep cover. Retains the strike with a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Pooja Vastrakar to Beth Mooney, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: At 115.7 clicks, on a hard length, angling in at the hips, Alyssa Healy gets inside the line and glances it down to fine leg for one more single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Pooja Vastrakar to Alyssa Healy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Offers width outside off, on a fullish length, Beth Mooney reaches out and knocks it to deep point for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Pooja Vastrakar to Beth Mooney, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off, Alyssa Healy waits on it and steers it with an open bat face towards third man for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Pooja Vastrakar to Alyssa Healy, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length delivery, around off, Beth Mooney uses her feet and strokes it towards extra cover where Shreyanka Patil dives to her right and keeps it to a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Pooja Vastrakar to Beth Mooney, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Short and punished! Pooja Vastrakar starts with a loosener, short and not much pace behind it, over middle and leg, Beth Mooney rides on top of the bounce and rolls her wrists to pull this one to the left of square leg for the first boundary of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Pooja Vastrakar to Beth Mooney, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Pooja Vastrakar to share the attack.

Gets the ball to angle back into the left-hander, on a good length, on middle, Beth Mooney is playing for the ball going away from her but adjusts well to cover the line of the ball. Gets an inside edge onto the front pad and the ball rolls in front of square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Slightly wayward from Renuka Singh as she slips this one short but wide outside off, Beth Mooney lets it go fo a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length, outside off, Beth Mooney gets on her toes and punches it on the bounce to backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drags her length back slightly and bowls it short, outside off, moving away, Beth Mooney reaches out to cut but does not go through with the shot as the ball goes past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Much better! Pitches it up, in the channel on off, Beth Mooney looks to get on the front foot to drive it down the ground but the ball angles away to go past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! At 105 clicks, on a length, swinging way outside off, left alone by Beth Mooney.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Renuka Singh to Beth Mooney, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Shaping into the batter, a bit too straight, on a length, on the pads, Alyssa Healy looks to help it away with the angle but misses out as the ball rolls off her pads to the left of Richa Ghosh for a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Renuka Singh to Alyssa Healy, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Alyssa Healy and Australia Women are away in this T20I series! Renuka Singh starts from over the wicket and serves with an upright seam, swinging in, on a good length, on the pads, Alyssa Healy lets the ball come to her and rolls her wrists to clip it through square leg for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Renuka Singh to Alyssa Healy, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! There is a light show going on at the stadium just before the start of the game. The India Women players are already out in the middle. Alyssa Healy and Beth Mooney are the two openers for Australia Women. Renuka Singh has the new ball and is raring to go. Let's play...

We are moments away from the first ball in this series opener, but before that, the match officials and the two teams will line up for the national anthems. It will be Australia's national anthem first, followed by the national anthem of India.

Shreyanka Patil is in for a chat. She says it is a special feeling to represent India and she has been dreaming of this moment since she was a kid. Shares that she rates herself as a strike bowler and she has a clear mindset of attacking the stumps. Further adds that she has trusted her processes and stuck to the plans. Feels that her execution was decent in the ODI series. States that Harmanpreet Kaur has given her freedom and she is enjoying it.

PITCH REPORT - Anjum Chopra is near the deck. She starts by informing that the straight boundaries are longer than the square ones. States that temperatures have gone down in Mumbai and feels that there will be a bit of dew. Mentions that both sides have quality pacers and spinners but reckons that the focus will be on the batters in this game.

The skipper of Australia Women, Alyssa Healy says that they are not too fussed but would have probably looked to bowl first as well. Mentions that they have a strong batting unit and they will look to put runs on the board. Shares that they have a lot of experience in their group and they know what to do in these conditions. Informs that Alana King and Kim Garth miss out from the team that played in the third ODI and Darcie Brown comes in as does Grace Harris.

The captain of India Women, Harmanpreet Kaur says that they will bowl first. Adds that they are going with 4 seamers and 2 spinners. Tells that they want to take this opportunity to try a few things in this series. Informs there are no debutants and they want to go with the same intent. Says the previous game did not go in their favour but Australia played some brilliant cricket and the only thing they can do is remain positive.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (C/WK), Beth Mooney, Tahlia McGrath, Ellyse Perry, Ashleigh Gardner, Phoebe Litchfield, Grace Harris, Annabel Sutherland, Georgia Wareham, Megan Schutt, Darcie Brown.

India Women (Playing XI) - Shafali Verma, Smriti Mandhana, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh (WK), Amanjot Kaur, Pooja Vastrakar, Renuka Singh, Shreyanka Patil, Titas Sadhu.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in the favour of Harmanpreet Kaur and India Women have opted to BOWL first.

Australia Women, currently perched at the top spot on the T20I Women's rankings, are a force to reckon with, which was on display during the ODI series. Despite a recent 2-1 series win against the West Indies, their T20I form was dealt a blow in the series against England, where they suffered a 2-1 defeat. That said, they have the upper hand over the hosts in this format and are the favourites to clinch the series. Will Australia continue their winning run and take the lead in the series? Let's find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly...

After a challenging ODI series where India Women faced a clean sweep at the hands of Australia Women, losing 3-0 in all aspects of the game, the T20I format offers a chance for redemption. Currently positioned at the 3rd spot on the T20I rankings, India Women aim to bounce back and showcase their prowess in the shortest format of the game. In their previous T20I series, they suffered a defeat with a 1-2 scoreline at home against England. Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. will have to step up in all three departments if they are to get the better of this formidable Australian unit.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the first T20I between India Women and Australia Women, set to unfold at the Dr. DY Patil Sports Academy in Navi Mumbai. As India Women seek redemption and Australian Women aim to assert their dominance, cricket enthusiasts can anticipate an exciting battle between bat and ball throughout this three-match T20I series.
... MATCH DAY ...

The stage is set for a thrilling T20 International showdown between India Women and Australia Women at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai. After the contrasting results in the Test and ODI formats, both teams will be eager to make their mark in the fast-paced T20 format. India, having secured a victory in the one-off Test, faced a setback with a 3-0 whitewash in the ODIs. India Women were close to winning the second ODI but had a dramatic collapse in the end. However, T20Is bring a different dynamic to the game, and the home team will be looking to bounce back. India would be keen to get a good initiation with bat from the dynamic Smriti Mandhana and will highly bank on the in-form and consistent middle-order sensations Jemimah Rodrigues and Richa Ghosh who will be crucial for India's batting line-up. Harmanpreet Kaur, the skipper, would look to contribute more with the bat after a dull series. Their ability to set the tone at the top of the order can play a pivotal role in determining the outcome of the match. India's bowling artillery includes the likes of Renuka Singh, Pooja Vastrakar, Saika Ishaque and Shreyanka Patil. On the other hand, Australia will be riding high on confidence after their dominant performance in the ODIs. The young and in-form Phoebe Litchfield, who showcased her brilliance with a century in the final ODI, will be their key player to watch out for. Ellyse Perry, Grace Harris, Alyssa Healy will be their key batters. The Australian bowling attack will rely on the responsible shoulders of skillful spinner Alana King, along with Georgia Wareham, Annabel Sutherland, Darcie Brown, and Megan Schutt who add depth and variety, posing a challenge for the Indian batters. As the cricketing giants collide in the T20 format, fans can expect a high-voltage contest filled with excitement, intense rivalries, and moments of individual brilliance. Strap in and get ready for nail-biting contests between these women's cricket heavyweights!
